Definition: from G5547; a Christian, i.e. follower of Christ:--Christian.
BiblicalUsage: The name Christian is given first at Antioch, by outsiders watching the disciples of Jesus. Agrippa uses it almost mockingly, asking Paul if he would persuade him to become one. Peter tells suffering believers not to be ashamed if they suffer as Christians, but to glorify God in that name.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the name was first a label from the world, and the church took it up as a badge of honour. To be called a Christian is to be named after Christ, and that is a name worth suffering for. My position is that the name still asks the same question Agrippa heard: does your life show whose you are?
